# Edge & API Gateways: Cloudflare, AWS ALB, Kong, KrakenD & Nginx (`edge-cloudflare-kong-krakend-nginx`)

> **Group:** II. Identity, Gateways & Multi-Cloud / On-Prem
> **Product Archetypes:** Cloud_Infra_IaC, OnPrem_Enterprise_Network
> **Trigger Signals:** cloudflare, kong, krakend, nginx, ingress, envoy, alb, waf, x-forwarded, gateway

## [ BLOCK: cloudflare-vs-bare-alb-origin-exposure ]
### Cloudflare Edge vs Bare AWS ALB / Direct Origin Exposure
- Check whether public domains route through Cloudflare WAF/Zero-Trust or expose bare AWS ALBs (`*.elb.amazonaws.com`), API Gateways, or public EC2/EKS IPs directly to the internet without WAF or rate limiting.
- Verify whether origin servers restrict ingress strictly to Cloudflare IP ranges / Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS), or if an attacker can bypass Cloudflare by hitting the origin ALB/IP directly.

## [ BLOCK: kong-krakend-nginx-header-spoofing ]
### Gateway Header Trust (`X-Forwarded-For`, `X-User-Id`, `X-Consumer-*`)
- Inspect `krakend.json`, `kong.yml`, `nginx.conf`, Envoy, or Kubernetes Ingress annotations for header forwarding rules (`input_headers`, `proxy_set_header`).
- Flag configurations where client-supplied identity/routing headers (`X-User-Id`, `X-Tenant-Id`, `X-Roles`, `X-Consumer-Username`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-Host`) are passed through to upstream services without being stripped/overwritten by the gateway.

## [ BLOCK: path-normalization-and-admin-port-exposure ]
### Path Normalization Bypass, Nginx `alias` Traversal & Admin Port Exposure
- Check for path parsing mismatches between gateway ACLs and backend routers (`/api/v1/public/../admin`, `/api/v1/admin;foo=bar`, URL-encoded `%2f`).
- Inspect Nginx `location` blocks for off-by-slash `alias` traversal (`location /static { alias /app/static/; }`) and exposed gateway admin APIs (Kong Admin `:8001`/`:8444`, KrakenD debug endpoints, Envoy `:9901`).

### Standard Mappings
- OWASP-API8:2023, OWASP-API9:2023, ASVS-5.0-V4-API-and-Web-Service, ASVS-5.0-V13-Configuration, ASVS-5.0-V14-Data-Protection, CWE-290, CWE-436, CWE-444

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- Origin ALB Security Group locked exclusively to Cloudflare IP ranges + Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS) or Cloudflare Tunnel
- Nginx proxy_set_header X-User-Id ""; / Kong request-transformer removing all client X-User-Id, X-Tenant-Id, X-Roles headers before injecting verified JWT claims
- Express app.set('trust proxy', ['10.0.0.0/8']) / Spring server.forward-headers-strategy=framework / Go trustedCIDRs restricted to known load balancer subnets
- Management and metrics ports (Kong :8001, Prometheus :9090, Spring Actuator /actuator, Envoy :9901) bound to localhost or isolated management VLAN
- KrakenD explicit input_headers allowlist (excluding internal X-User-* / X-Tenant-* headers) combined with auth/validator JWT signature and scope enforcement on every endpoint
- Nginx location blocks using matching trailing slashes on both location /static/ and alias /var/www/app/static/; with merge_slashes on and normalized URI routing

### Vulnerable Patterns
- Public AWS ALB (*.elb.amazonaws.com) or origin public IP reachable directly on 0.0.0.0/0, bypassing Cloudflare WAF and bot/rate limits
- KrakenD input_headers: ["*"] or Nginx passing client-supplied X-User-Id, X-Tenant-Id, X-Forwarded-For directly to backend microservices
- Nginx alias path traversal (location /static { alias /var/www/app/; } missing trailing slash) or URL decoding disparity (/api/v1/public/../admin/users) bypassing gateway ACLs
- Kong Admin API (:8001/:8444), Spring Boot /actuator/env, or Envoy /stats exposed on public ingress routes
- Dynamic Nginx proxy_pass http://$http_x_target_host; or KrakenD backend host interpolation allowing unauthenticated SSRF into internal VPC services
- HTTP/1.1 Transfer-Encoding / Content-Length desynchronization or h2c (HTTP/2 cleartext) upgrade passthrough at reverse proxy allowing request smuggling across backend connections

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of nginx.conf, krakend.json, kong.yml, Envoy config, or Kubernetes Ingress manifest showing route and header rules
- ev_... excerpt of Terraform/CloudFormation ALB, SecurityGroup, or Cloudflare origin rules showing network exposure
- ev_... excerpt of backend middleware reading X-Forwarded-*, X-Real-IP, X-User-*, or X-Tenant-* headers
- ev_... excerpt of gateway authentication plugin config and admin/metrics port listener bindings

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Are AWS Security Groups or NACL rules restricting the ALB ingress to Cloudflare IPs only, or is the ALB directly reachable from 0.0.0.0/0?
- Does the upstream API Gateway strip all incoming X-User-* / X-Tenant-* headers before forwarding?
- Are path normalization and reject-encoded-slash rules consistent between the edge gateway (Kong/Nginx/ALB) and the downstream framework?
- Are gateway admin interfaces (Kong :8001, Envoy :9901, Actuator) blocked at the Kubernetes Service / Ingress layer?
